paper.citation: Calonico, S., Cattaneo, M. D., and Farrell, M. H. (2018). On the Effect of Bias Estimation on Coverage Accuracy in Nonparametric Inference. Journal of the American Statistical Association 113(522), 767-779. DOI: 10.1080/01621459.2017.1285776.
paper.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
paper.source_locator: Supplement S.II.7 (Complete Simulation Results), printed p.80, PDF p.81: data-generating process Y=m(X)+eps, X~U[-1,1], eps~N(0,1), and Model 1 regression function m(x)=sin(4x)+2*exp(-64*x^2). Main text Section 4 (Simulation Results), printed p.776, PDF p.10: the five-point evaluation grid x in {-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3,2/3}.

mechanism.name: Nonparametric regression with sine plus Gaussian bump: CCF2018 Model 1 (m(x)=sin(4x)+2*exp(-64x^2))

generation_equations.label: DGP structure
generation_equations.expression: Y = m(X) + eps,  X ~ U[-1,1],  eps ~ N(0,1)  independently of X

generation_equations.label: Even-part identity
generation_equations.expression: m(x) + m(-x) = 4*exp(-64*x^2)  (sin cancels as odd; bump doubles as even)

assumptions: iid observations; X is independent of the noise eps
eps ~ N(0,1) with mean zero, so E[Y|X=x0] = m(x0) is deterministic and known in closed form
m(x) is smooth (infinitely differentiable); the Gaussian bump 2*exp(-64*x^2) is centered at x=0 with effective width ~1/8 and creates high curvature near x=0
Pointwise inference at each fixed query point; the five-point grid is NOT evaluated as a simultaneous confidence band by the current scalar truth interface
No causal interpretation; this is a nonparametric regression inference (NRI) task with no treatment, mediator, or intervention

properties.notes: Univariate nonparametric regression (dimension=1, effective_dimension=1: one covariate X fully determines the conditional mean). Nonlinearity from two sources: (i) the sinusoidal oscillation sin(4x), which completes roughly 4/(2*pi) ~ 0.64 of a period over [-1,1]; (ii) the sharp Gaussian bump 2*exp(-64*x^2) centered at x=0 with effective width ~1/8. The bump dominates m(0)=2 and is negligible (<=1e-12) at |x|>=2/3. No interactions, no high-dimensional structure, no irrelevant padding.

estimand.name: m(x0) = E[Y | X = x0]
estimand.definition: Conditional mean of Y given X = x0 at a fixed query point x0 from the grid {-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3,2/3}, in the superpopulation defined by Y = m(X) + eps, X ~ U[-1,1], eps ~ N(0,1). Model 1: m(x)=sin(4x)+2*exp(-64*x^2), a sine oscillation plus a sharp Gaussian bump centered at x=0. Each query point is a separate pointwise inference target; the five points are not a simultaneous confidence band.

parameters.description: CCF2018 S.II.7 Model 1: m(x)=sin(4x)+2*exp(-64*x^2), query x0=-2/3

truth.expression: Conditional mean of Y given X = x0 at a fixed query point x0 from the grid {-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3,2/3}, in the superpopulation defined by Y = m(X) + eps, X ~ U[-1,1], eps ~ N(0,1). Model 1: m(x)=sin(4x)+2*exp(-64*x^2), a sine oscillation plus a sharp Gaussian bump centered at x=0. Each query point is a separate pointwise inference target; the five points are not a simultaneous confidence band.
truth.derivation: Direct analytic/numerical evaluation of m(x0)=sin(4*x0)+2*exp(-64*x0^2). At x0=0 the value is exactly 2.0 (sin(0)=0, exp(0)=1). At x0=+/-2/3 the Gaussian bump contributes <9e-13 so m(x0)=sin(4*x0) to machine precision. At x0=+/-1/3 both the sine and bump contribute. Independent verification uses an even-part identity m(x)+m(-x)=4*exp(-64*x^2) (the odd sine cancels, the even bump doubles) and a separate arithmetic path.

adaptations: Model 1 is a sine-plus-Gaussian-bump regression function newly constructed by CCF2018 (distinct from the Hall-Horowitz 2013 damped-sine family g2/g3); registered as an independent mean family as specified by the task.

The five evaluation points {-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3,2/3} are registered as separate fixed-query-point scenarios because the current scalar truth interface returns one m(x0) per call; each is a pointwise 95% interval target, not a simultaneous confidence band.
Population truth is computed by direct analytic/numerical evaluation (closed-form function); no coverage simulation, bootstrap, or PFN training is run in this collection.
